(a) Deval made an offer dated 1st February 2026 to Elemi for the sale of his car. The terms of the offer provided thus: price, 5 million; acceptance, in a fortnight; delivery of the car, two days after payment. Seven days after the offer, Ekpe agreed to buy the same car from Deval for 7 million and the latter hurriedly posted a revocation letter to Elemi on the 8th of February terminating the offer. Initially Elemi rejected the offer through a letter he posted on 5th of February 2026. After a careful commercial introspection Elemi changed his mind and being oblivious of the revocation by Deval, Elemi wrote and posted an acceptance letter to Deval on the 13th of February 2026. Meanwhile, Ekpe has paid and collected the car from Deval. Identify all the legal principles in this case and advise all the parties as to their legal rights/obligations in this transaction.

(b) Mr Imoke sold Motorcycle to Mr Aji at 1 million Naira with the agreement of collecting a monthly sum of 100 thousand once Mr Aji's salary is paid. Few months afterwards, salary was not forthcoming due to government delay in receiving allocation. He explained to Mr Imoke who then agreed for a lesser sum of 50 thousand to be paid monthly. Can Imoke turn around to insist on his strict legal right to 100 thousand Naira as well as claim arrears?

(c) Mr Eno is a notorious coupon player. He filled a coupon in respect of a pool on football matches organized by AJA Pools. He predicted the scores of all the matches correctly and therefore was entitled to 10 million. AJA Pools has refused to pay Mr Eno a dime arguing that they are insulated from legal liability by reason of a clause in the coupon contract which states that, 'the transaction was binding in honour'. Mr Eno is oblivious of this clause and AJA Pool just paid Mr Okon 10 million for correct prediction in the same matches. Mr Eno is contemplating on commencing legal action against AJA Pools. Advise Mr Eno. Would your answer be the same if the defendant's representation is a mere puffs?

Elemi, a minor, an undergraduate student of UNILAG, entered into a leasehold agreement, (for an apartment) with Gersh Henshew Housing for 1 million. He paid 600,000 and occupied the apartment for six months. He decided to transfer his studentship to UNIABUJA, hence he seeks to repudiate the household agreement and to recover the consideration furnished in the transaction. Advise the parties. What if Elemi is a drunkard or a mentally impaired person who bought food items on credit at exorbitant rate from Mrs Susan? Is the legal protection afforded illiterates a shield or sword? (15 marks)

Musa is a wealthy trader in Port Harcourt who owns several properties. He approached Grace an illiterate widow and asked her to sign a document he claimed is a tenancy agreement for the small shop she is leasing from him. The document was a sale agreement for transfer of ownership of Grace's land. She relied on his representation before thumb -printing it. Later that evening, he met Shola at a party where he was intoxicated and barely coherent. Musa convinced him to sell his power bike for 50,000 naira only. The next morning, Shola refused to deliver the bike to Musa. Discuss the validity of the contracts with Musa. Would your answer be different if Musa was not aware of Shola's state of mind? (15 marks)

Ekpo hired a car from Bassey for a trip from Calabar to Lagos and paid the full fare for it. Two minutes after take-off, the engine of the car caught fire and Ekpo and his wife were partly burnt. There was no fire extinguisher and the contract agreement signed between them contained no statement that the car would be safe and suitable. Ekpo has engaged a lawyer to sue Bassey. Applying the relevant authorities, state how this problem will be solved. (15 marks).

Also on Friday, Chief Pemu and his wife travelled from Benue state to Calabar, checked into Cannan City Hotel and paid the charge of N30,000 on the ground floor at the reception to cover two nights. In the evening when they went downstairs to the restaurant to have a meal, the cashier saw them and gave a receipt for the N30,000 which they had paid for the accommodation. The receipt contained a notice disclaiming liability for guests' articles that may be lost or stolen. The following day, they went out in the morning to attend the wedding ceremony. After the church ceremony, they rushed to the Hotel to take the gifts and some money to give at the reception, only to discover that the wedding gifts and the entire sum of N500,000 had been stolen from the hotel room. Chief Pemu has consulted a Lawyer on the matter. What relevant issues and authorities will be applicable? (15 marks).

(a) Discuss the principles and rules employed by the courts in restricting the scope and effect of exclusion and limiting clauses, illustrating your answer with authorities. (7½ marks)

(b.) Distinguish between representations, warranties and conditions, illustrating your answer with authorities. (7½ marks)
